query: For multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures, what single testable methodological intervention could overcome the inability of EAM references to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid? Explain why it should improve reference–target phase-space overlap, predict the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, define the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identify supporting evidence from elemental or binary calculations, and specify a decisive free-energy benchmark that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Replacing traditional EAM references with a deep-learning-based interatomic potential—trained using an active-learning framework on ab initio solid and liquid configurations—will yield a more faithful representation of the diverse atomic environments in multicomponent high-entropy alloys near their melting temperatures. This improved representation enhances the phase‐space overlap between reference and target systems and reduces the mismatch in the thermodynamic-integration path relative to TOR–TILD’s EAM references.
generation.material_initial_state: Multicomponent high-entropy alloys (containing 4–6 principal elements) in both their solid and liquid states, studied at temperatures from approximately 0.8 times the melting temperature (Tm) up through complete melt.
generation.intervention: Implement a deep neural network force field trained via an integrated active-learning strategy on high-fidelity ab initio data covering both solid and liquid configurations. This single methodological change replaces the limited EAM reference potential.
generation.conditions: The approach is applicable to HEAs with 4–6 principal elements under extreme thermal conditions near melting (from ~0.8 Tm to full melt), where the atomic configurations are highly diverse.
generation.structural_mediator: The flexible, data-driven potential functional form captures many-body interactions and local coordination variations present in both phases, mediating an improved mapping between the wide configurational space and the computed forces/energies.
generation.mechanism: By using a training dataset that actively targets underrepresented atomic configurations (via active learning), the deep-learning potential accurately reproduces the ab initio energy landscape. This leads to superior phase-space overlap with the target system and a smaller integration path mismatch, as the potential can adapt to the high configurational disorder inherent in the ab initio liquid.
generation.predicted_outcome: The intervention is expected to reduce the mismatch in the thermodynamic integration path relative to TOR–TILD’s EAM references, yielding free-energy differences that agree with ab initio benchmarks within the nominal uncertainty. Although the exact quantitative reduction is uncertain, the ML potential should display statistically significant improvements in configurational sampling and energy accuracy.
generation.baseline: The current state-of-the-art using traditional EAM references (TOR–TILD’s EAM) that suffer from inadequate representation of the many atomic configurations in high-temperature, multicomponent liquid states.
generation.boundary: This method’s effectiveness is primarily expected for systems with 4–6 principal elements near their melting temperatures. Its performance may be limited for alloys with extreme chemical complexity beyond these regimes or if the ab initio data is insufficiently diverse to capture all relevant configurations.
generation.uncertainty: While prior elemental and binary studies and recent work on high-entropy carbonitrides support the potential of deep-learning methods, the exact reduction in thermodynamic integration mismatch is uncertain and may depend sensitively on the quality and diversity of the ab initio training data.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct parallel thermodynamic integration workflows for a representative multicomponent HEA (with 4–6 elements) at temperatures from ~0.8 Tm to full melt. One workflow employs the deep-learning-based potential while the other uses the conventional EAM (TOR–TILD) reference. Free energies will also be computed directly via ab initio methods for benchmark comparison.
measurements: Thermodynamic free-energy differences along the integration path
Metrics of phase-space overlap (e.g., configuration distribution overlaps)
Error bars relative to ab initio benchmark uncertainties
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the free-energy differences obtained with the ML potential do not show a statistically significant reduction in integration mismatch compared to the EAM reference—or if the phase-space overlap metrics are not improved relative to ab initio data—then the hypothesis is falsified.

The melting temperature together with supercooling and superheating temperatures of a number of high-entropy carbonitrides (TiZrTaHfNb)CxN1−x with different concentrations of carbon substituted by nitrogen are calculated. The deep learning DeepMD potential is trained on the number of DFT calculations in order to accurately describe both the liquid and solid phases of the considered high-entropy carbonitrides. A new computational procedure is developed and applied to determine the melting hysteresis and melting temperature of HECN using active learning techniques. Heating and cooling curves for HECNs are calculated and carefully analyzed in order to determine the main trends in changes of melting temperatures with respect to nitrogen content. Pair correlation analysis is employed to explain the enhancement of the melting temperature of carbonitrides with small amounts of nitrogen. The obtained data indicates the potential of applications of high-entropy carbonitrides as promising hard and refractive materials for protective coatings of various equipment which operates at extreme conditions.

decision.trend: Early work on high-entropy alloys focused on experimental demonstrations of enhanced mechanical, thermal, and magnetic properties but largely relied on classical, relatively rigid empirical potentials (e.g., EAM) for simulations. While these methods offered initial guidance, they struggled to capture liquid-state disorder and the highly varied local configurations in multicomponent systems near melting. More recent efforts have turned to machine learning-derived or deep neural network interatomic potentials as showcased by the melting simulations of high-entropy carbonitrides, where the improved flexibility of these ML potentials enabled faithful representation of both solid and liquid phases across wide composition/temperature ranges. Despite these advances, fully integrating such ML-based potentials into accurate thermodynamic-integration workflows for multicomponent alloys remains an open challenge.
decision.unsolved: A persistent obstacle is establishing a robust reference potential that faithfully reproduces ab initio forces and energies over the broad configurational space of high-entropy liquids near their melting points. Classical EAM references have proven inadequate due to their limited functional form, resulting in significant thermodynamic-integration path mismatches. Although recent studies demonstrate the promise of ML potentials for single-phase or nearly isotropic systems, their performance across very high temperatures, multiple phases, and diverse alloy compositions, as well as systematic free-energy verification against ab initio data, remains to be conclusively shown.
decision.lever: Train and validate a deep-learning-based interatomic potential (e.g., a neural network force field) on high-fidelity ab initio data capturing both solid and liquid configurations near the melting range for representative multicomponent alloys. Key parameters include an integrated active-learning strategy for robust sampling of high-entropy configurations, coverage of 4–6 principal elements, and temperatures spanning ~0.8Tm through the complete melt.
decision.why: Building on recent success in modeling HEA melting with deep-learning potentials, this approach can directly address the limitations of EAM references by accurately reproducing a more diverse set of local coordination environments. It is expected to improve reference–target phase-space overlap and reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatches relative to EAM-based TOR–TILD by constructing a flexible, data-driven representation that adapts to the high configurational complexity. The applicable composition range is any multicomponent alloy (4+ constituents) that forms HEAs in both solid and liquid states, and the relevant temperatures extend from near solidus to above the liquidus. Supporting evidence comes from earlier demonstrations of neural-network-based potentials for elemental and binary systems, as well as the deep-learning study on high-entropy carbonitrides. A direct comparison of free energies derived via ab initio thermodynamic integration versus those obtained from the new ML reference potential under the same conditions would serve as a definitive benchmark: a discrepancy larger than the expected uncertainty in the ab initio data would falsify the hypothesis.
